title: First Light oncall snapshot — 2026-05-20
content:
Summary:
First light shift (03:00-11:00 UTC) handed over. Quiet first three hours, then a transient API tail-latency spike affected a subset of /v1/generate requests from hosted-api (p95 jump from ~120ms to ~1.2s). No user-facing errors observed; increased latency produced timeout retries in a downstream customer integration.

What happened (timeline):
- 03:12 UTC: Observability alert: p95 token latency > 800ms for route /v1/generate (hosted-api-west).
- 03:14 UTC: Pager to oncall. Began investigation (metrics + traces).
- 03:18 UTC: Traces show heavy KV-cache miss ratio on a small percentage of hosts (region-west-a).
- 03:22 UTC: Noticed recent autoscaler activity + burst capacity allocation around 03:10; new nodes joined but had an out-of-sync KV-cache warmup path.
- 03:35 UTC: Mitigation: temporarily routed traffic away from affected pool via router override (policy -> fallback pool), p95 recovered to baseline by 03:45.
- 04:05 UTC: Removed override after coordinated cache pre-warm job ran; monitored for recurrence — none in shift.

Impact:
- Scope: ~0.7% of total requests in region-west during incident window.
- Customer-visible errors: none confirmed, but one partner reported increased client-side retries that correlated with the window (ticket: JIRA-REL-321).
- Cost: minor (brief extra autoscaler activity), no billing anomalies.

Immediate actions taken: 
- Router override to fallback pool to restore latency.
- Triggered cache pre-warm job for the new nodes.
- Rolled back a recent experimental node-init flag in the canary pool (flag: node-init-async-ttl).
- Notified Platform Eng and Serving Runtime teams in #sre-ops and #platform-alerts; paged Marco for kernel-selection telemetry help.

Root-cause hypothesis:
- New nodes were joining with node-init-async-ttl enabled; the async path deferred prefix/KV warmup causing initial high miss rates under load. Autoscaler burst + routing caused a spike when the new nodes received traffic before pre-warm completed.

Follow-ups / action items (owners & ETA):
- Disable node-init-async-ttl in autoscale image pipeline until we have safe warmup gating (owner: Priya K, ETA: 2026-05-22).
- Add a pre-warm stage to the autoscaler lifecycle that blocks routing until KV-cache health probe passes (owner: Platform Eng, assignee: Marco C, ETA: 2026-05-27).
- Update runbook: "Serving node warmup" to include detection and router override checklist and example `curl` probes (owner: Aisha B, ETA: 2026-05-23).
- Post-incident review doc + RCA (owner: Aisha B, collaborators: Evan O'N, ETA: 2026-05-25).

Runbook draft notes (to incorporate before next incident):
- Add clear detection thresholds for KV-cache miss ratio (suggested: >10% sustained for 2 minutes on any host).
- Standard operating procedure: immediate router override to fallback pool -> mark affected hosts draining -> trigger pre-warm -> validate p95 and trace patterns -> reintroduce hosts after two golden intervals.
- Example commands for engineers (router override, drain, pre-warm job invocation) to be copy/pasted into runbook.

Open tickets created during shift:
- JIRA-REL-321: "Partner observed retries during west region latency spike" (linked).
- SRE-OPS-114: "Add autoscaler warmup gating" (created by Marco).

Handoff notes for next shift:
- No ongoing incidents. The router override has been removed and affected hosts are green.
- Follow-ups listed above remain open; Priya will lead the immediate config lock (patch), Marco will own gating work.
- Watch: autoscaler activity in west region for next 48h while rolling the image change; set alert to lower threshold for cache-miss ratio during node joins.

Operational suggestions / improvement ideas:
- Consider a brief cold-start buffer: autoscaler should maintain a 1-minute staging window where new nodes receive health-check-only traffic.
- Instrument node-init to emit detailed warmup progress events into metrics (so we can alert on slow warmups automatically).

Notes to self (Aisha):
- Log snippets saved to /srv/ops/logs/2026-05-20-west-kvmiss.log and attached to JIRA-REL-321.
- Slack thread: #platform-alerts thread id: CA12345WQ (link in artifacts).

Retro on handoff quality:
- Runbook gaps made initial TTR longer than ideal; mitigation steps were straightforward once cache miss was identified.
- Suggest a one-paragraph checklist pinned to the SRE channel for fast router override steps.

If anything regresses, contact me (Aisha) directly in #sre-ops or page Evan (mobile available).

End of snapshot.
